obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers must conduct real-world testing of high-risk AI systems only in accordance with Article 60 and a real-world testing plan, without prejudice to prohibitions under Article 5.
exceptions: Does not apply to high-risk AI systems related to products covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, which are subject to separate Union or national law.

obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers must draw up a real-world testing plan and submit it to the market surveillance authority in the Member State where testing is to be conducted before commencing real-world testing.

Providers or prospective providers must obtain approval from the relevant market surveillance authority for the testing in real world conditions and the real-world testing plan before conducting such testing.
exceptions: Where the market surveillance authority does not respond within 30 days, approval is deemed granted by tacit approval, unless national law does not provide for tacit approval, in which case explicit authorisation is required.

obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers must register the testing in real world conditions with a Union-wide unique single identification number and the information specified in Annex IX, in the EU database or secure non-public section as applicable to the AI system type.
exceptions: Providers of high-risk AI systems under Annex III points 1, 6, and 7 in law enforcement, migration, asylum, and border control must register in the secure non-public section of the EU database per Article 49(4)(d); providers under Annex III point 2 must register per Article 49(5).

obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers conducting real-world testing must be established in the Union or appoint a legal representative established in the Union.

Providers or prospective providers must ensure that data collected and processed for real-world testing is transferred to third countries only where appropriate and applicable safeguards under Union law are implemented.

Providers or prospective providers must ensure that real-world testing does not last longer than necessary to achieve its objectives and in any case no longer than six months, extendable by a further six months only upon prior notification to the market surveillance authority with justification.
exceptions: An extension of up to six additional months is permitted upon prior notification and explanation of need to the market surveillance authority.

obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers must ensure that subjects of real-world testing who belong to vulnerable groups due to age or disability are appropriately protected.

Where testing is conducted in cooperation with deployers or prospective deployers, providers or prospective providers must inform them of all relevant aspects of the testing, provide instructions for use per Article 13, and conclude a written agreement specifying roles and responsibilities for compliance.
Providers or prospective providers must obtain informed consent from subjects of real-world testing in accordance with Article 61 before commencing such testing.
exceptions: In law enforcement contexts where seeking informed consent would prevent the AI system from being tested, the testing and its outcomes must have no negative effect on the subjects, and their personal data must be deleted after the test.

obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers, as well as deployers or prospective deployers, must effectively oversee the real-world testing through suitably qualified persons with the necessary capacity, training, and authority.
Providers or prospective providers must ensure that the predictions, recommendations, or decisions of the AI system during real-world testing can be effectively reversed and disregarded.

Providers or prospective providers must allow subjects or their legally designated representatives to withdraw from real-world testing at any time without detriment or justification, and must promptly and permanently delete their personal data upon request.
exceptions: Withdrawal does not affect activities already carried out before revocation of consent.

obligations.summary: Providers or prospective providers must report any serious incident identified during real-world testing to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73, and must immediately adopt mitigation measures or suspend or terminate the testing.
Providers or prospective providers must establish a procedure for the prompt recall of the AI system upon termination of real-world testing following a serious incident.
Providers or prospective providers must notify the national market surveillance authority of the suspension or termination of real-world testing and of the final outcomes.
Providers or prospective providers are liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage caused in the course of real-world testing.
